name: Responder
what: A network poisoner for LLMNR, NBT-NS and mDNS with rogue authentication servers (SMB, HTTP, LDAP and others). It captures NetNTLM challenges when Windows clients try to resolve names that do not exist on the network.
when: In an authorized internal assessment or purple-team exercise to measure how many systems still fall for broadcast name resolution, and to prove the value of disabling LLMNR/NBT-NS and enabling SMB signing / EPA.
example: Clone the active repo on an assessment VLAN you control: `git clone https://github.com/lgandx/Responder.git`.
Start in analyze mode first so you only observe queries: `python3 Responder.py -I eth0 -A`.
With explicit approval, enable poisoning on that interface and collect hashes only from in-scope hosts.
Feed captured NetNTLMv2 hashes into an offline cracker in your lab (for example Hashcat) and report which systems still broadcast LLMNR/NBT-NS.
pitfalls: Active poisoning can break name resolution for nearby users; use a dedicated test VLAN when possible and keep the window short.
The SpiderLabs fork is deprecated; use lgandx/Responder.
Capturing credentials for accounts outside scope is still a breach of engagement rules; filter and destroy out-of-scope material.
